name: submit_training_recommendation
content:
{
  "headline": "Your strength is declining across all lifts; rest and recovery must be your priority now.",
  "summary": "This period shows a concerning pattern: strength indices have dropped significantly across chest, back, legs, and shoulders, while you report joint pain, fatigue, and declining session quality. Despite logging 56 sets and solid volume distribution, the objective data confirms your subjective experience—your body is signaling overtraining or accumulated fatigue. This is not a programming failure; it is a recovery failure. The good news is that deloading now will protect your long-term muscle-building goal and likely restore your strength within days to a week.",
  "progressiveOverload": {
    "status": "regressing",
    "notes": "Strength indices dropped across the board this period. Chest fell from 105 to 99, back from 104 to 98, legs from 104 to 97, and shoulders from 103 to 99. Only biceps and triceps remained relatively stable (100 and 100 respectively). These declines are significant and consistent, indicating systemic fatigue rather than a single weak lift. Progressive overload has stalled and reversed."
  },
  "muscleImbalances": [],
  "deloadRecommended": true,
  "deloadReason": "Multiple strength indices have declined significantly across major muscle groups despite reasonable volume. Combined with your report of joint aches, feeling run down, and worsening session performance, this is textbook overtraining or inadequate recovery. A deload will reset your nervous system and connective tissues, allowing you to return to progressive overload with better results and longevity.",
  "actionItems": [
    "Take a full deload week: reduce volume by 40-50 percent and lower intensity to 6-7 out of 10 effort, focusing on movement quality and mobility rather than load",
    "Prioritize sleep, nutrition, and stress management—aim for 8+ hours of sleep and ensure you are eating enough calories to support recovery and your muscle-building goal",
    "After the deload, return to your previous progression scheme but monitor your subjective recovery weekly; if fatigue returns, increase rest days or reduce weekly volume by one session",
    "Get bloodwork done if joint pain persists after deload, as persistent aches combined with sudden strength loss may indicate underlying deficiency or health issue worth checking"
  ],
  "contextSummary": "Strength declined across all major lifts despite solid volume; user reported fatigue and joint pain, signaling need for deload and recovery focus before resuming progression."
}
